title: Operational Runbooks as Living Documents: A Longitudinal Study of Document Evolution under Assisted Post-Incident Revision
abstract: arXiv:2611.29097v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Operational runbooks increasingly function as living documents within operational workflows: they are maintained by people, used in incident support, and continuously revised as organizational knowledge changes. Yet little is known about how such document collections evolve over time in production settings, or which interpretable signals are useful for monitoring document change. We analyze 17 weeks of version-controlled runbook snapshots produced during post-incident revision with machine-assisted review and human oversight. We quantify document evolution using lightweight linguistic and structural signals grounded in prior work on procedural language, technical communication, and document organization. Correlation analysis shows mixed patterns of association, including both positive and negative relationships, with effect sizes ranging from negligible to moderate and varying across corpora. translated_title: 作为“活文档”的运维手册：辅助式事后修订下文档演进的纵向研究
translated_abstract: 运维手册在运维工作流中日益发挥着“活文档”的作用：它们由人员维护、用于事件支持，并随着组织知识的变化而持续修订。然而，目前鲜有研究了解这类文档集合在生产环境中如何随时间演进，以及哪些可解释的信号对于监控文档变化是有用的。我们分析了17周内版本控制的运维手册快照，这些快照产生于机器辅助审查与人工监督之下的事后修订过程。我们基于先前关于程序性语言、技术沟通和文档组织的研究，采用轻量级的语言学与结构信号来量化文档演进。相关性分析显示出混合的关联模式，包括正相关与负相关关系，其效应量从可忽略到中等不等，并在不同语料库之间存在差异。时间维度的摘要分析进一步区分了……
tldr: 该论文首次对生产环境中运维手册作为“活文档”的长期演进进行了纵向实证研究，并提出利用轻量级的语言学与结构信号来量化与监控文档随时间的变化。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a longitudinal empirical study of how operational runbooks evolve as living documents in production, introducing lightweight linguistic and structural signals to quantify and monitor document change over time.
